chapter: Arranging career and the JPJ Quartet
title: Writing for Ina Ray Hutton and Boyd Raeburn; Jimmy Noone's influence
summary: Budd and Dizzy write for Ina Ray Hutton and Raeburn, and Budd says Benny Goodman's clarinet sound derives from Jimmy Noone, for whom Budd wrote.

bands.name: Ina Ray Hutton and Her Orchestra

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: So with Ina Rae Hutton, I forget what I used to write for her, but I used to -- Dizzy Gillespie was writing for WHEN Boyd Ina Rae, I was writing for Ina Rae, she would come in. Board Rabin, Dizzy Gillespie, Tad Damon and myself, we were --and I don't want to forget this guy's name, I'll recall it in a Boyd Rabin minute. We were all writing for Board Rabin. Jimmy Noone --
well, that was back in the Chicago days -- He was one of the -- Ben Goodman's influences.
You better believe it. You know, Benny Goodman tried to --

-- emulate this man's sound. This man had one of the greatest sounds on the clarinet, and even when you hear Benny Goodman play 'Sweet Lorraine' today you'll hear Jimmy Noone. That was Jimmy Noone's cri p.
Right. That means it was his best song.

Yeah, he could really play this song, and which is not an easy song to play, especially when you get into the channo. You better know your right changes. But Jimmie Noone, he was such a great guy and I wrote some things with him. I don't -- whatever he asked me to write because I used to play with him in Chicago.
You had permission to write these things, yes.
